newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul protests to Japan over fishing boat seizure.
newsitem.headline: Seoul protests to Japan over fishing boat seizure.

text.p: South Korea on Wednesday summoned Tokyo's ambassador to Seoul to protest at the seizure of one of its fishing boats by Japanese patrol vessels in disputed waters, a Seoul foreign ministry spokesman said.

Vice Foreign Minister Lee Ki-choo called in the envoy, Shintaro Yamashita, to lodge a formal protest over Tuesday's seizure and to demand steps to ensure such an incident is not repeated, the spokesman said.
Japan last month held four South Korean fishing boats for intruding into its recently expanded territorial waters.

"A new fisheries agreement is being negotiated between the two countries and our position is that the existing agreement, which has been in force for over 30 years, must be observed," spokesman Lee Kyu-hyung told Reuters.
Japan last January expanded its territorial waters in accordance with a new maritime convention introduced by the United Nations in November 1994, he said.

Japan and South Korea have a troubled relationship stemming from Japan's brutal 1910-45 colonial rule over the Korean peninsula. Frequent territorial disputes are fanned by ultra-nationalists on both sides.
